utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone and I'm glad that everyone has been able to make it, despite this very wet weather. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Matthew Olmsted, Joanna Korner, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, and Katarina Danicic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I given to understand that there are a number of preliminary matters which -- with which we'll deal before the witness returns?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, can I deal with my first two short matters, first of all, but I need to deal with it in private session, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber by majority, Judge Harhoff dissenting, agrees to the admission of the document as being admitted -- which is now admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D352, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Now could the usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I note for the record that Tom Hannis has joined us in the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Aleksandar Aleksic, who joined the team during this break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, good morning to you. As a matter of courtesy, I should --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As a matter of courtesy I should explain to you that the reason for the delay in your -- the continuation of your testimony this morning was that the Court was dealing with a number of procedural issues, but now Mr. Zecevic may resume his cross-examination. Before he does so, I remind you you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. May the usher provide the witness -- a statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, yesterday we spoke about Kotor Varos. I showed you some documents, and now I want to move on to another municipality, namely Zvornik. Unless I'm mistaken, in your schematic, you mentioned two cases of -- or two instances of crimes against non-Serbs in the municipality of Zvornik, and that is mentioned in the KU register; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't able to identify these instances, but I will try to do so now with your help. We'll see whether the KU register corresponds to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 1D002398, tab 38 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here this is an official note of the first instance court of Zvornik about the murder of two persons by identified perpetrators. The two victims are Avdurahman Haskic and his wife Zuhra Haskic. By their names, I conclude that they are Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since this is the document of a court, it is marked KRI-22/92; 92 being the year, and the date is 20 June 1992. Is this crime entered in the register of the SJB of Zvornik which you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say for certain, because under 1 in the register of crimes a murder is entered but three victims are mentioned. Maybe a mistake was made so that the reporting person was also entered as a witness. But anyway, under this number in the KU register I see three victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Maybe I can interject, maybe try to be a little bit helpful with this. If you have a KU or crime register number available, if you can give us that, that's the way we can check with the crime register and see if there is an entry for it. Otherwise, this witness, without having the register in front of him, it's hard for him to verify if this entry goes to this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Olmsted, this is precisely my question, whether this -- this event, this criminal event, the murder of two non-Serbs, has been entered in the KU register, because what we have here is the court document. So it would normally be -- in the normal circumstances there should have been a KU entry and then the criminal complaint, criminal report was filed with the Prosecutor, and then the court would -- would be involved in this -- in this matter. And that is precisely what I am trying to find out from the witness, and I don't have the KU number for this because even the witness cannot identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, that's my point, is -- as we know, the -- the crime register contains a listing of all the reports filed by the police. So if the police did not file a criminal report with regard to this incident, it wouldn't be in the crime register, and so just -- sometimes you're talking about apples and oranges. If you're talking about an on-site investigation, we don't know whether it was investigated by the police, and if you do have that information and you do have a KU number, that would be helpful and that's how we could link it to the crime register, and that's the only point I wanted to raise with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me the witness wants to it say something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the crime register of Zvornik, under 1, the murder of three victims was entered, and under number 63, the murder of three victims is also entered, but their identity could not be established from what is entered in the register. Maybe we can check that. So it's a KU 1 and KU 63, these two entries.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I note that the witness is referring to the unrevised annex, and perhaps I can provide him with a revised annex so that we're reading off the one that's the most current.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] KU 1, three victims in the revised version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We'll need some time to find the numbers in the KU register of Zvornik, and then we'll get back to this. Tell me, in the KU register for Zvornik, did you see any crime of rape where the perpetrator is a Serb and the victim a non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's KU 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What date is that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this overview there are no dates but just the number KU, and the crime, and who the perpetrator was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does it have to do with Zdravko Cvoric's case?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that because I don't have the overview of Zvornik in front of me. If we could show the Zvornik KU or if I could see the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if the Prosecution have that with them, then perhaps they might assist the witness, that's the Zvornik register.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: In fact, I do have this particular register, and I will provide it. I'm just wondering how fruitful this will be if we go along this course. This witness obviously had a limited task with regard to the crime registers, and so he's not going to be able to speak to great lengths about the cases, but he certainly can, as an example, show where this one is in the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may just explain. The witness was show the KU registers. When we talked yesterday, the witness and myself, he confirmed that these KU registers by themselves are not sufficient to establish with sufficient certainty what the Prosecution wants to establish in this case. I am now specifically showing the witness that there are documents which confirm that criminal proceedings were conducted against persons in the municipalities which he looked over and that this was not entered in the KU registers. So this was situation where, in fact, criminal proceedings were conducted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please proceed along your course, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, here's the Zvornik crime register. We'll give it a number of 10495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under KU 27 -- just a second. A person -- how do you say, Zdravko Coric as the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The 3rd of August, 1992. And let us not mention the name of the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And under KU 1, as we said, three victims, murder. It is not the case which you showed but the case dated the 4th of May, 1992, and the following persons were murdered: One Croat and two Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us then go back to the case 1D00-2398, which we can see on the screen. Sir, this is an official note drafted at the it basic court in Zvornik. On the right-hand side of the Zvornik we can see the employees of the Public Security Station Zvornik, one Delic, Vlado, an inspector, and Damjanovic, Dragomir, who is forensic technician. This is an official note that has to do with the on-site investigation in relation to the murder of these two persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As an official note was drafted by the basic court and as the Judge who was on duty was present, it is undoubted, as this is a crime which is prosecuted ex officio, it is undoubted that the event should be included in the KU register; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as to why this was not done? I mean, I'm not asking you to speculate. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D353, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My apologies, Your Honours. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we compare it with the crime of rape, that is to say the case against Zdravko Coric, you have established that it is entered in the KU register; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just for the sake of reference, this is document 65 ter 2114. For the sake of the completeness of the witness's testimony, I would suggest that this document also be tendered. It is a case file from Zvornik and has to do with the crime perpetrated by Zdravko Coric, rape against a person of Muslim ethnicity. If there are no objections, would I tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You said for completeness. We -- aren't we in danger of redundancy, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is a million dollar question, Your Honour. I fully agree with you. The fact that the document is in the KU report is sufficient for me. I was just thinking that it might not be bad to have this one just to fulfil the picture, but I would understand the position of the Trial Chamber fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think we could do without this one, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I understand. [Interpretation] Could we now please show the witness 1D04-2290.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, if I understood -- that's tab 40. I apologise. If I understood you properly a second ago, you said that in your chart you came across one crime of rape committed by a Serb against non-Serbs in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we have found that case file. I just showed it to you a while ago. Now you can see in front of you a request to open investigation, which was drafted by the basic prosecutor's office in Zvornik because of a crime committed on the 20th of May, 1992, also a rape committed by one Zoran Tomasevic, and the damaged party is the underaged member of a non-Serb ethnic group. Can you confirm whether this crime is registered in the KU register from Zvornik or not?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This request does not ask for the investigating judge, that is to say the prosecutor doesn't refer to the KU number, but this crime was committed in Bratunac, so most probably this crime was registered in Bratunac. I say most probably because I haven't examined their books, but it cannot be excluded that the criminal file was submitted at the prosecutor's office and that then the prosecution requested that investigation be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as the witness examined the document which Mr. Olmsted presented to him and which is in front of him now, that's 65 ter 10495, I am of the position that possibly we should include this document in the evidence, though I wish to it hear the Prosecution's position regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And before we hear the Prosecution's observations on the matter, I would wish to just put one question regarding the date, because it appears that the murder took place on the 20th of May, and there was a criminal report on the 25th of May, 1992, but the request appears not to have occurred until a year later, namely 26th of May, 1993. Is there any explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Which murder are you referring to? You mean the rape or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Yes, yes, yes, the rape, yes, sir. I'm referring to the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. Well, in this request to open the investigation, the public prosecutor from Zvornik on the 26th of May, 1993. Maybe that's a mistake, I'm not sure - files the -- the request to open investigation for the crime that happened on the 20th of May, 1992, a crime of rape. That is -- that is what I can read from this document, Your Honour. And I'm not sure I follow the discrepancies on the dates that you were mentioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I can also read from the screen, and I was just putting a question as to why was this request made only one year later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably the public prosecutor can answer that, but I can ask the witness, Your Honour, if -- if the witness is able to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have heard the question. Can you please answer.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One the reasons why the request was sent again to the investigating judge only one year later is the place of birth and residence of Zoran Tomasevic. He was born in Pancevo in Serbia, and probably the prosecution organs could not get hold of him. And that was probably why the prosecutor's office waited until the presence of the suspect was certain. So that's one of the reasons that could have caused such a delay. And that happened in the entire area of the former SFRY. The identity of the perpetrator was perhaps established as soon as the crime was reported, because the damaged party may have known him personally, but maybe he was at large all the time from the date when the criminal file was submitted to the date on which this request to open investigation was submitted by the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, do you have a view on Mr. Zecevic's application?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes. If the application is with regard to the Zvornik crime register 10495, we have no objection for it being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, was that your application?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your microphone isn't working.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was referring to the -- I don't know if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the actual KU book from Zvornik which Mr. Olmsted -- thanks to Mr. Olmsted, was provided to the witness, and the witness consulted that document in order to be able to give us the answers and enlighten us on these documents which I presented to him. That is why I felt it is needed that this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So it is this document, the 10495.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is, correct, 65 ter 10495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And then what about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The one on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the witness explained, I believe, why this document was not entered in the KU register of Zvornik because the place where the rape was committed belongs to the territory of another SJB, and that is why I didn't thought there was enough nexus to offer that document for admittance. But would I gladly do that if the Trial Chamber would want me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Vasic, we will move to another municipality. This time, Pale municipality. Can you please find it in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this document should be returned to the Prosecution. [In English] Could the usher please help and return the document to Mr. Olmsted. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The microphones are a bit odd today. Just to note for the record, this is also, I believe, a revised annex. So the witness should refer to the revised annex that we offered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, unless I'm mistaken, your chart says that the KU register of the public security station Pale does not contain any crime in which the perpetrators were Serbs and the damaged parties were non-Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that there are two crimes in which the damaged parties are non-Serbs and the perpetrators are unidentified. In both cases this is the crime of murder under Article 36 of the Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a total of four victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Four victims in total?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I see in your statement something for which I need an explanation. I'm referring to your statement. Let me find the exact date. A statement dated the 31st of March and 1st of April this year, item 24. You say that you reviewed the KU register of the SJB of Pale from 1992 and you say: "In this crime register, I wasn't able to find any crimes that are mentioned in the annexes to the indictment."

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was requested to check whether some crimes or incidents that caused great harm were processed, but there were no -- no such in that register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Unless I'm mistaken, and I don't think I am, the indictment in this case only mentions two instances of murder in the territory of the Pale municipality in 1992, with two victims. And here we see that it was entered that two murders had been committed with a total of four victims, four non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it says that the crimes were committed but not entered, but such offences cannot be found here, only such as were committed and entered in the KU register. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of which, the situation is the same in the Bijeljina municipality. In your schematic for the Bijeljina municipality, we see two criminal offences in the KU register of the SJB of Bijeljina where the perpetrators were Serbs and the victims non-Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One murder and one extortion. Items 224 and 297, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But in your statement that we have just seen, dated 31 March and 1 April this year, and that is item 27 of your statement, you say once more that you have examined the KU register for the CSB and the SJB of Bijeljina and say: "In this KU register, I could not find any criminal offences that are mentioned in the annexes to the indictment." Since in the annexes to the indictment not one crime committed in Bijeljina is mentioned, I would like to know what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is a bit confusing for this witness, because there's two issue at stake here, because the witness was asked to look at two different things separately. First, he was given our indictment and the annexes to our indictment, as well as another -- another form that brought in all the various crimes that are in those schedules per municipality, and he was asked first to identify whether any of the of crimes that we specifically mentioned in the annexes, or in our schedules of our indictment, he could find any criminal reports for those. The second part was with regard to serious crimes. These annexes in the revised annex for Bijeljina deals with serious crimes. It does not address crimes alleged in the schedules of our indictment, and that really is the explanation for why there are two different things. But I think the witness is confused because you're kind of conflating the two, what's in our schedules versus what is a serious crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I may respond. It was not at all my intention to confuse the witness. I am only asking, because I do not understand the comment made by the witness in his statement under 27, his statement of 31st and the 1st of April of this year, 31st of March and the 1st of April, where he said he could not identify in the records, in the KU book, any of the crimes alleged in the indictment, but there is no crimes alleged in the indictment in Bijeljina. Not a single specific crime has been alleged in your indictment against our clients in this case in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now I understand my learned friend's point and let me correct him that we do charge Bijeljina in the indictment. We charge Batkovic detention facility, which was in Bijeljina, as well as it does fall within the general persecutory count, count 1. So that is the scheduled crime that was at issue for this first part of his task. The second part of the task was with regard to serious crimes and that's what this annex refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could you attempt your question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you heard what we said. I'm confused by your statement where you say in item 27 that you weren't able to find any crimes with which I totally agree, since not one particular crime from the territory of Bijeljina municipality can be -- is -- correction, is mentioned in the indictment. What Mr. Olmsted is saying about the military camp of Batkovic is something else altogether, and clearly we cannot expect the opening of the camp or anything of that kind to -- to be entered in the register.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in this table of crimes that may be found in the KU register, we could see the places where something happened or whether there is intelligence about that, and I said whether I found it there or not. And the crimes themselves are mentioned in the register. But I don't have all these documents, so maybe that's why this resembles a Chinese whispers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just explain to me one thing. Did the OTP tell you to look for information about crimes committed at specific places, or did you do it based on the intelligence that the MUP of the RS has?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The OTP gave me a table where some places and events are mentioned, and they wanted me to check whether these were investigated and entered in the relevant registers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you received a table from the OTP mentioning particular crimes, and they asked you to check whether they are entered in the KU registers of the MUP throughout the RS.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Olmsted, I'm indeed quite surprised that we never received that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, you do have the document. That might be an oversight that I did not include it with his 92 ter package. It is included with the -- I believe it's ST-136 is 92 ter package. All it is is taking the schedules which are arranged by category of crime or detention facility and putting in by municipality, because the witness had to review the log-books municipality by municipality, so it made sense that he looked at them from the perspective of -- rearranged the schedules in a way that made it easier for him to do that. We certainly can provide that to the Defence. During the break, I will give you a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you provide we can discuss this during the break so we don't use the valuable court time. However, if you can provide with the 65 ter number of this document so we can put it on the -- on the monitor. And -- and the part which refers to Bijeljina, territory of SJB Bijeljina so witness can comment if that is the document which he had in mind -- which he was talking about. [Interpretation] Perhaps we can return to this issue after the break once we -- once the relevant documents are ready. And I can move on to something else, or perhaps have the break a bit earlier, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we're just two minutes away, so it is probably a convenient point to break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm waiting for the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness, do we correctly -- is our arithmetic correct that this witness, we aren't going to complete this witness until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It appears so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, since we solved the issue of Bijeljina during this break, we will move on to the following municipality I would like to speak about with you, and that is Doboj. If I understood probably, in your diagram you state that at the SJB and at the CSB of Doboj there was one crime committed by a Serb where the victim was a non-Serb.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it before me. Maybe we could see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's Annex 15. I can give you my copy if you want.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in your diagram it reads that you established that the KU -- in the KU registers for the CSB and the SJB of Doboj there is only one crime entered which was committed by a Serb against a non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is KU 64, entry KU 64, in the SJB of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And these -- and this crime is?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a -- it's the crime of murder as entered in the KU register of the SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the OTP now please assist us concerning 65 ter 10493, please. In my conversation with the Prosecution before resuming, we established that this document was wrongly scanned and put into e-court as such, which makes it impossible for the witness to look at it in e-court. Therefore, the Prosecution agreed to put the document on Sanction, for which I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes. In the interim, we've directed the problem and it's in e-court and now 65 ter number 10493, and it's on the screen right now. And, Mr. Zecevic, the record says that this KU entry 64 was for the crime of murder. I'm not sure if that was misstated or what, but I think the crime was for rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I heard the witness said the rape, and about the -- about his answer concerning the eight crimes of the unknown perpetrators were murders, but maybe witness can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the crime entered under KU 64 at the SJB was an instance of rape, and eight crimes committed by unknown perpetrators that are entered in the register of the CSB were instances of murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Let us now look at the crime register which we have before us. There are eight instances of murder committed by unknown perpetrators against non-Serbs. If I followed attentively, this refers to the entry starting from 11/92.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eleven, 12, 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the relevant page on e-court where the entries 11, 12, and 13 can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I think if you just turn to the next page that should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Eleven, 12, 13. These are the first three entries on this page. Then 16. That's the sixth entry, and 18, the eighth entry. They are all committed by unknown perpetrators, that is "NN," and are marked red.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps rotate the image.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To rotate it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a suggestion, if my colleagues from the Prosecution agree. We can save some time. I have here 15 documents from the public security station and security services centre in Doboj. These are documents which are on our list, tab 41 until and including tab 55. I suggest, Your Honours, that I should give all these 15 documents to the witness and let the witness establish on the basis of examining these documents whether any of them, any of these criminal files, are included in the crime register, and then we might show only the ones that are not included in the crime register to the Trial Chamber and tender them into evidence. I think that in this way we might significantly shorten the time that we need for the questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I don't object to that procedure. I've been informed that there is a problem with e-court, so let's publish the log-book on Sanction now so that he can review the log-book as he goes through the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And while you are -- while you are putting the Sanction on, may the usher give this to the witness, if it pleases the Court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have now given you 15 documents, criminal files from the public security station and security services centre in Doboj, with the names of the damaged parties. I would ask you to review these documents and check them against the list which is on the screen in front of you so that all those which are recorded in the crime register do not have to be shown to the Trial Chamber. And as for the ones which are not there, we will show them and then tender them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, can I ask you how long will this take the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe two more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that is substantially shorter than if I would present document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's not -- I don't have a problem with it. I was just wondering whether it would be appropriate to ask him to do that in the break we have to take in a few minutes, or even right now. Could he do it in that break?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, Your Honour. Maybe that's -- that's even better.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: The only problem is -- is that we only have an electronic version of this log-book. I don't have a hard copy of it. If we can set him up somewhere with e-court, that probably won't be a problem. Obviously I can't interact with him, so I'm not sure how that can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand from the Registry that the problem has been corrected with the version on screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Perhaps since we've been moving back between Sanction and e-court, maybe we can just stay in Sanction for now. Does that cause any -- oh, I see. It's in e-court. So that's fine. So we can go back to e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, maybe I can ask my assistants to print out the relevant pages of the -- of the KU book and then we give the witness at the break so we don't lose any more time. And I will provide the copies to the Registry and then the Registry can give it to him through the Victims and Witnesses Unit. And we take the break now so Your Honours can deal with the ex parte.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's one of those days, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: When it rains, it pours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to the cover page or the first page so that I could see numbers from 1 to 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's proceed with the cross-examination. We need another five to ten minutes before the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness the first page of the crime register with the numbers 1 to 10. Did I understand you properly, that that's what you need?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There it is. Would you like us to zoom in?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second page once again. The previous page, please. Can we show the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, with regards to this book, and I discovered this last night when I was reviewing some of the documents the Defence has proposed for cross-examination, I noticed that the first page of this log-book is missing from the exhibit. Now, that could be one of two things. One, it could have been a bad job of photography in that when the investigators went out to take photographs of this log-book that they missed the first page or the first page simply doesn't exist. What we can do is go back to Doboj and check to make sure that the page is either missing, or if it wasn't photographed properly to rephotograph it to be included in the exhibit. This is an error, obviously. The investigators were photographing thousands and thousands of log-book pages and sometimes something goes missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One of those days you said, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vasic, I apologise. Such things happen. If you can, try and help us. I don't know if you can give us the answer without reviewing the page which we obviously do not have.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the first page we have three crimes of murder committed in two cases by unidentified perpetrators and in one case by identified perpetrators. These are numbers 5 and 6 with the unidentified perpetrators, and KU 7 is the number under which there is a murder of a non-Serb committed by a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. But these three instances which you enumerated now on the first page are not in your schematic?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So your schematic as compared to the numbers should be modified, and these three entries under numbers 5, 6, and 7 should be included in it. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please give back the documents to me.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I state which ones are recorded in the register?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: First please return these three which are not there so that we can tender them into evidence and then we shall slowly move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness just gave me three documents. These are tabs 45, 47, and 48, and the documents are criminal reports dated the 3rd of August, 1992, 1D03-1240. As the witness has reviewed the documents, I think that there is no need to show them in e-court again. Unless there are any objections from the Prosecution, I would suggest that they be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I recommend a different course. As I suggested that the Prosecution goes back and determines whether there is, in fact, a missed page in the log-book, and if we can find that page to admit that page along with the log-book itself so you have a complete log-book, and there you can see for yourselves entries 5, 6, and 7, rather than admitting documents that really don't relate directly to this witness's testimony. Since he can't speak about the cases themselves, he just simply reviewed the log-book. And that will make it clear that his analysis left off that first page because it was simply missing from the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But with all due respect, Your Honours, these documents, they contain the reference KU 5, 6, and 7, and the witness testified to that. So it would be much shorter way to introduce these three documents. I don't have anything against, but if we are to ask the Prosecutor, the investigator goes to Doboj and photocopies the first page, then we will have to return the witness for the -- for continuance of the testimony. I think this is a much shorter cut and much shorter way of introducing these documents and having the full picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That wasn't my recommendation to have the witness return, it was simply to admit the log-book itself into evidence and then we will report back whether the page exists or it doesn't. If it does exist, we'll just add that to the exhibit so that you will have the complete exhibit with the missing page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So you agree with the application to admit the log-book?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: To admit the log-book, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And we appreciate that this matter of the missing page we are going to have to return to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. I will ask that the log-book be admitted that has been agreed with the Prosecution, but what I want is to admit these three documents which are relevant to our case and which do not exist in the existing log-book because of the missing first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we would admit the documents, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Your Honours. Let me read the documents. The first one I read -- please bear with me, Your Honours. The first -- the first one I read was 1D03-1240. That is the criminal complaint of 3rd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D355, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The second document is -- is the document 1D01-0307. That is a criminal complaint filed on the 8th -- on the 1st of August, 1992, and it's recorded on the face of it as KU 5/92.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And this will be Exhibit 1D356, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the last document is 1D00-3668. It's the criminal complaint filed on the 1st of August, 1992, and on the face of it it's been recorded in the KU log-book as number 6/92.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And this it will be Exhibit 1D357, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, perhaps it would be good to have it on the record. You did not mention the KU number for the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, that is correct, Your Honours. I failed to do that. The document which is admitted as 1D355 has a KU number 7/92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I move the Trial Chamber now to admit the log-book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The log-book for SJB Doboj is 109 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It's -- it's the CSB Doboj log-book, and it's 10493.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D359, Your Honours. Yes, Your Honours. 1D358.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 1D358 is 65 ter 10493. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vasic, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document which you showed here connected with the number KU 16/92 is mentioned in the overview. Then KU 18/92 also. 24/92 as well, a murder. Security services centre was in charge of that. 29/92, 31, and 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you managed to identify among these documents those which have been included in the KU register as well in your schematic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please return these documents to me.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now we will move to the last group of documents.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand that they're ready for us to do the other work with which the Chamber has to deal now, so perhaps this would be a suitable point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have to rise, and it seems to me that you should think in terms of returning at the time when we would have resumed for the final session that's at 12.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we are about to go into closed session. We will resume in open session at 12.25. The Bench need not rise in order to accommodate this. So ... I should add it's a closed session to deal with an ex parte situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we reconvene in open court, and I invite Mr. Zecevic to resume his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Vasic, although it has nothing to do with me, but the situation is just like that. We broke off when we were dealing with the documents from Doboj from that set of documents that I gave you. Could you explain the situation with the documents you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents have no KU entry number, so probably they weren't entered, and the CSB sent them to the basic public prosecutor's office in Doboj. The authenticity of the documents can only be established for -- by conducting a check at the public prosecutor's office, and the crimes involved are causing general danger with lethal consequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. You'll just give it back to me.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't find these documents in the KU register because there's no mention on the documents that they were entered there, and that was not the usual practice. What was sent to the prosecutor's office should have been marked "KU."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the usher to return the documents to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was speaking about document KU 29, that it was entered in the register. Could you -- could I see it again so we may check whether it was indeed entered, because 24 was, but I'm not sure about 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you want to see it on the screen again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D358 in e-court, the page with item number 29. And could the usher please return this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before going to that, would I like to ask the witness, the previous documents you gave back to Mr. Zecevic, you said you couldn't identify them as being in the KU register. My question is: Are they not, or are you not -- are they not in that register, or are you not able to identify and to tell us whether they're in the KU register or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If these reports were filed in the register, we would have found them because these are serious crimes, and they would have been included in the statistics, although they were not marked as KU. In the statistics, it would have been clear that they were entered in the KU register because these were serious crimes that were involved, causing general danger with lethal consequences involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you say they are not in the KU register; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I see KU 29? Although the description reads "Inflicting serious bodily injuries," but if this was entered in the register, then it isn't included in the statistics because there is no mention of lethal outcome of the injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please see 1D358 on the screens for the witness to see. We need the page with entry number 29. My guess is that it's on -- oh, here it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It mentions serious bodily injuries. That's why it isn't included in this analysis. If there had been -- if these injuries had resulted in death, it would have been clearly stated in the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have the document back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood properly, the document under tab 52, 1D01-0321, and that's a criminal report dated 20 November 1992, against unidentified perpetrators, and the victim is Ismet Hrnjadovic, obviously a Muslim who died of the consequences, so this document can be found in the register.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's marked 29 through 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But since you were unable to establish by looking at the register that this person died, you didn't consider the crime committed so serious as to be included in your schematic. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now that you have looked at this document, you think that this document should be included in the schematic that you attached to your statement.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would have been good, because that would have completed the information. Serious bodily injury with lethal consequence within 24 hours, that can even be qualified as murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line with this comment, Your Honours, I seek to tender 1D01-0321 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D359, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now return to the documents that you gave back to me a minute ago. They're also from Doboj. The first one is 1D01-0311. You're about to see it in e-court. By reviewing these documents, namely this one and the following five, that -- and you established that for some reason these documents were not entered in the KU register, although they should have been given their nature.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document that we see on the screen is dated 22 August 1992. It's a criminal report for murder. We see that the perpetrator is NN. That is, unidentified. And the victim is one Husein Colic. Judging by his first name, he is a Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is also a serious crime, murder. So that by applying these criteria, we can conclude that if it had been in the KU register, it would have been included in your schematic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender document 1D01-0311, and that is tab 41, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D360, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The following document, 1D01-0313, tab 42. This situation is the same as with the previous document. It's dated 24 August, 1992, a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator or several perpetrators for murder, and the victim is Esad Saracevic from Doboj. Judging by the first name and the last name, too, we can conclude that he is a Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again if this document had been entered in the KU register, you would have included it in your schematic because since it's about a serious crime, it should have been included in the schematic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D361, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The following document, 1D01-0315, tab 43. This is about -- actually, this is an on-site investigation report. Let me be very precise now. On the first page of the letter which the CSB Doboj sent out, it is signed by the chief of the centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. It was sent to the public prosecutor's office. It's about the case of Bozidar Vidovic and others, who are Serbs, and it's about the activation by an antitank mine at Svjetlici, which is probably a village in the Doboj municipality, as a consequence of which Sejfudin Hodzic died on the spot, who is also a Muslim. And one Mirsad Durmic sustained serious injuries, also a Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If this document had been entered in the KU register due to the seriousness of the crime and the lethal outcome of the action, it would have been included in your schematic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I speak to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your -- Your Honours -- Your Honours, I look at this document and I don't see a crime. I see the people died because they ran over a mine, so I'm not sure it really establishes what the Defence is attempting to establish with it. We need further evidence that this was, in fact, a deliberate crime committed by someone. It could be simply an accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted echos the Chamber's query, Mr. Zecevic. What is your response?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The allegation by the Prosecution was there was a discriminatory policy of the MUP of Republika Srpska during 1992 where all the cases or the criminal acts or deaths of the Muslims were not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We haven't lost sight of that. The narrow question is whether this particular incident constituted a crime or as Mr. Olmsted said was an unfortunate accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I ask the Defence again to please refrain from especially speaking about what the Prosecution's case is purportedly to be when the witness is present. I think that is an issue for argument at the end of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was only trying to explain. Your Honours, the point of the matter is that this document has been sent by the CSB to the public prosecutor. So therefore there has to have been a certain criminal procedure before the prosecutor, otherwise these documents would not have been sent to the prosecutor. That is my explanation. Maybe -- maybe the witness can help with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, certainly you can ask the witness, but I think he's already established that he doesn't have any personal knowledge about these various cases as far as the representation as to why this was sent to the prosecutor, that again would probably require a degree of speculation on the part of this witness given he doesn't know anything about this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So on the face of it, Mr. Zecevic, this doesn't relate to a crime, and it seems that it would -- is therefore not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the following document: 1D01-0309. That's tab 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is again a letter sent to the basic public prosecutor's office. The date is the 10th of August, 1992, and the security services centre in Doboj is submitting to the basic public prosecutor's office in Doboj the official note drafted at the site of a fire at Jozo Barukcic's house. On that occasion, the owner of the house, Jozo Barukcic, lost his life. He died because of the injuries he sustained. It is not mentioned that criminal proceedings have been initiated, but it is a fact that some sort of investigation had to be conducted in case when the death of a person occurred. It had to be done ex officio; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Regardless of whether it was an accident, a suicide, or a murder, an investigation would be conducted, though in case when death was the result of an accident or if someone committed suicide, then a report would be submitted to the Prosecution to decide. So it is important for the investigative judge and the prosecutor's office to conduct an investigation and decide whether there are any elements of a crime or not. If there was no suspicion that this was arson, certainly this would not be registered in the KU register, but it would be normally recorded at the prosecutor's office. So there was an investigation, and if during the on-site investigation it was established that this person burnt himself, whether because there was a problem with heating or because there was some other failure and then the person suffocated and whether it was a suicide or if the person was murdered, if he was not murdered then it would not be registered in the KU register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, this document shows that the police, that is to say the Doboj CSB, conducted an investigation of the death of Jozo Barukcic - I believe that he is a Croat - regardless of the results that they established at the end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, regardless of the results that they established, it is up to the prosecutor to decide what sort of proceedings would be initiated once he received the documents which members of the Ministry of the Interior submit to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree that we really do not know whether this was a crime or not. However, it was the death of a Croat. As the witness confirmed, the police conducted an investigation, and from the moment when the documents were submitted, it was in the hands of the prosecutor's office and not the police. Therefore, I believe this document to be relevant and I suggest that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, well, of course I won't raise the same objection I raised before, but in addition, all this witness is doing is looking at this document and reading what it says and agreeing with what the Defence is asking. So I don't think it's adding anything to admit the documents itself into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, the question I was going to ask is isn't this the same type as the last document, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Qualitatively speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that there is similarity between the two documents, but still, Your Honours, with all due respect, the proposition which we think is relevant is which -- which the witness confirmed, is that the -- is that the police has done its job concerning the death of the person of the other ethnicity. In 1992 reported that, conducted an investigation, and gave the file to the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: In relation to crimes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but we don't know if this was a crime or not, because the investigation might -- might have developed that it was -- that the fire was set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The point is is it in the KU register or not, and what the witness says basically, if it's not a crime, it's not in the KU register. So because if it is not in the KU register, you could -- you could conclude that it is not a crime. But in any event, it doesn't prove anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So why should we admit it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I fully agree with Your Honour, but as you have seen from the previous documents, there have been criminal complaints, obviously crimes of murder, which have not been recorded in the KU, and that is the whole point, because what we say is what the witness confirmed to me at the very beginning, that the KU register alone is not, is not to be trusted fully to show the -- the situation as it was. That is why I am going through this -- through this exercise, Your Honours, and I think it's relevant, and of course we intend to rely on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not a criminal report. This is information going to the prosecutor's office. What follows is the witness says there is an on-site investigation. If there is evidence of a crime, the police have to investigate it, file a criminal report. So there's a whole procedure that must follow this, and therefore this is simply one page and it doesn't tell us anything beyond what the witness has told us, which is the police have a duty to investigate and report things to their prosecutor. So why it's not in the crime register, this witness cannot explain. Maybe there was never a criminal report filed on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I explained why this is not in the register, because deaths which are the result of accident or suicide are not entered in the register. They are recorded in the usual clerk's office which is present in each police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: For the same reasons why the previous document we declined to admit it, we decline to admit this. Mr. Zecevic, in terms of the evidence that the Chamber has heard, which as we understand is directed to establishing the -- that the KU register on which the Prosecution relies is not wholly accurate, that is -- appears to be incontrovertible at this point, and we wonder on that basis how many more like specimens you intend to tender in support of this proposition which the Prosecution, as I appreciate the evidence, is not in a position to refute as a basic principle? We know that there's room for argument in terms of the effect of all of this, but in terms that the KU register was not wholly accurate, that seems to be fairly well established.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have only one more document, which is a criminal complaint, and I think it's irrelevant for this particular municipality. However, the next municipality that I have, it is my understanding that the KU register was never shown to the witness, and therefore I intend to introduce these documents in support of the -- of our position that the -- that the police in that particular territory, in that particular municipality, which is in our indictment and in the relevant time, were performing their duties in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let's move, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness 1D00-6974.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in a few seconds you will see this document on the screen. It's under tab 46. This is a criminal report submitted by the Doboj CSB on the 3rd of August, 1992, against known perpetrators, four of them. Three were fully identified, and the fourth one was partly identified. All of them Serbs. The crime that they are charged with is murder, and the victim is Ivan Cigoj, a Croat, and Ferid Cabric, who I suppose is a Muslim. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have established that this criminal report, even though it should be included in the crime register in Doboj, maintained by the Doboj CSB, has not been entered in it, and as this is a serious crime, it should also be included in your schematic; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had been recorded in the K register, it would be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D362, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- was it then included in the K register?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The witness -- the witness confirmed that this entry, this criminal complaint, was never reported in the KU register although it should have been, in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is the difficulty of this inquiry without the witness seeing the entire documents and the log-books. For instance, when I was reviewing this document last night, I noticed it appeared to be related to another document on the Defence's document list, 1D03-1240, which appears in the crime register under entry 7/92. Now, if they're related cases, it's just simply another criminal report regarding the same criminal incident, then it would be in the same entry for that crime register. So it's very difficult for the witness to sit here today and say, Oh, this criminal report is not linked to another entry in the crime register without seeing the files, without looking at the crime register and making that determination. So I think there is a limit to the amount of information this witness can provide on-the-spot notice in cross-examination without all the information he needs to make that assessment. Maybe the Defence can confirm that those two criminal reports are related, the one that is under KU 7/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If my recollection is right, the KU 7/92 was not recorded previously by the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That was because of the missing page in the log-book which we will look into.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe when we have the complete log-book maybe we can discuss this some more. And with all due respect, Your Honours, the witness is the Prosecutor's witness, and he was asked to comment on the documents he has never seen before, and he produced the charts and the diagrams based on these documents. So I don't see any difference from what I'm doing and what the -- what the Office of the Prosecutor was asking this witness to do, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think Judge Harhoff has really hit the nail on the head. If we have a KU number, then it's quite easy to go to the log-book and say, Yes, this witness misidentified it. He should have included it in one of his annexes. But without a KU number, we have a criminal report here. We don't know if it was filed. We don't know what happened do after it was written. We don't know if it's in the crime register because we don't have a cross-reference number. So really the witness would have to look at this criminal report, at the criminal report under KU 7/92, determine whether they're the same entry or they're really the same criminal transaction and say, Yes, it is recorded in the KU. It really does take a little bit of a further development which I think for the purposes of this witness, which is simply looking at the crime register and saying, Yes, I can see from this document that this log-book, that these are crimes committed against non-Serbs, I think that's really the extent what he's trying to do. As far as showing him criminal reports or case files and asking him to link them to the log-books, well, that does require considerable effort on his part here on the stand to do that, and unfortunately Defence is not really giving that full opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I just complete. Maybe we have a different interpretation of the witness's answer, but -- but my remark was prompted by the witness's response to your question, Mr. Zecevic, the response on page 12, line 22, in which the witness says that if the incident had been recorded in the K register it would be there, presumably in the KU log-book. It's just -- so my question was, well, was it then registered somewhere? That remains, as I understand it, an open question. The fact remains that, yes, the police did do its work in the sense that a criminal report was made, as we see it in front us, and so the only question that remains is whether the -- the investigation that was made and initiated by the police in Doboj, whether that was recorded in one or some other log-book, and that's where I'm still uncertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well -- but that is precisely, Your Honours, what my -- what our complaint on this exercise of the -- of the Office of the Prosecutor is, because we say that by analysing only the KU register, the -- the real situation will not be established, because as we -- as I mentioned yesterday with the witness, there is a book of -- of on-site investigation. There is a daily log-book. We hear now that there is a normal log-book where -- where all other documents are recorded such as the documents which you denied the admittance which I showed just -- just couple of minutes ago. So therefore, what we are saying is that in order to -- for the -- for the Office of the Prosecutor to establish what they tried to establish, they will have to bring all these documents together and then invite us to draw the conclusions. That is the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But the Presiding Judge's remark a while ago still stands, namely that evidence has been provided to show that the KU log-book in itself is incomplete to understand the full picture, and I think this is accepted by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well -- well, I'm perfectly satisfied, because the whole exercise what I'm -- what I am performing is aimed to show Your Honours that that is the fact, and that is why I'm showing these documents, in order to establish that some of the documents which normally and according to the law should have been entered in the KU register were, in fact, not, which does not mean, as the Office of the Prosecution is suggesting, that the police was turning a blind eye against the crimes for non-Serbs, but are, in fact, the result of something completely different, situation or --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is better suited for argument, not while the witness is here testifying. I think Your Honours are correct, that that is one piece of evidence in the Prosecution's case. Obviously the Prosecution has presented a whole number of different types of evidence which we hope the Trial Chamber will look at as a whole to try to understand the picture of what was happening back then, but beyond that I don't think it's necessary to go into more oral argument as to what the evidence shows or what it doesn't show or what the Prosecution's position is or what it isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I would like to go back to that last document with the more or less -- with -- the witness's answer was not very clear to us, so the question is to the witness: Were you able to say that this crime, the crime in that last report that was -- that was discussed, was not in the QA -- the KU log-book? Was that what you were telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, the way it is is not marked KU, so based on this I can only say that it cannot be found in the KU register. Would I have to review the entire KU register once more to try to find whether it is entered anywhere, and if so, under which item number. So from the statistics that I have, I can say that there has not been one single case of a murder of a group of non-Serbs by Serbs. Based on the documents that I had at my disposal, I can say that this kind of report is not entered in the KU register. However, it may be one of the entries from 1 to 10, because I've never seen them. But as it isn't marked KU, the validity of this document must be checked with the public prosecutor's office of Doboj, because the question arises now whether this document was sent to the prosecutors at all. It may have remained at the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is Your Honour satisfied with the answer, or should I ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether this was sent to the public prosecutor's office or not is a matter of speculation. I cannot claim either that it was or that it wasn't based on the document as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, the essence of what you're trying to say is that it is necessary to review the log-books of the public prosecutor's office at Doboj to find out which criminal reports were received by that office; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the best way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since we have spoken about the inadequacy of the KU register ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since, as I said, we spoke about the inadequacy of that register as the only indicator, I would like to show you P405. It's a document which is a report about the audit of the SJB conducted by the CSB, dated 22 October 1992. It's a report drafted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
