utterances.text: Let me remind you this document is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. I wasn't aware that this document was confidential at all. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps then we shouldn't show the document to the witness. I will just read to him the relevant paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 5, which is page 7 of the English text of this document it says -- this is the report prepared by the -- by the workers of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. [Interpretation] These people from the ministry, when they audited the CSB, found out the following, it was established, and I quote: "That at the CSB Doboj, no register exists about the reception of criminal reports, the so-called KU register, although they were warned at the beginning of August to do so. They were given an extended deadline until the 22nd of August to do so and retroactively enter all criminal reports, as well as enter them in the operative register." Does this clarification shed any light on the situation with the KU register at the SJB of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, because the ministry headquarters was duty-bound to control the work of the lower-ranking organisational units such as the police administration and the criminal police administration and check, in the course of such audits, whether or not the laws and regulation were is being abided by, and based on that, instruct the centres and the stations to eliminate any possible shortcomings. If the shortcomings were more serious, they could launch disciplinary proceedings against the responsible persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to me, sir, that at the beginning of your reply you said that some of the KU registers were never shown to you. I believe that you were unable to find them. I think you mentioned Vogosca and Kljuc, among others; right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vogosca, Ilijas, Kljuc, and I can't remember the fourth municipality now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that Vogosca under the Dayton Accord became part of the federation?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same with Vogosca and Ilijas. And I think that there's also Hadzici. The same case -- the same applies to them. And in 1995 they became part of the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in all these cases we can assume -- well, actually, I don't want to have you speculate, but in most of these cases were you -- or, rather, where no KU registers were found, that was at the SJBs which under the Dayton Accord became part of the federation?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO VASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kljuc immediately before the Dayton Accord and these three after.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For that reason I must show you some documents from Kljuc so we may establish whether or not these documents, given their nature, were such as to be entered in the KU register.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: As my learned friend has established, there -- the crime register for this municipality could not be located, so this witness, given that he's already stated that he doesn't know -- he has no personal knowledge of what was happening in other municipalities beyond Laktasi, I'm not sure that this is going to be useful for the Trial Chamber to show him a bunch of criminal reports that have no association with any log-book that he's reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I take -- I take the argument from my learned friend to be of some substance. I do agree, to a certain extent, but, Your Honours, Kljuc is one of the municipalities in the indictment. These are the criminal reports and the documents prepared by the police at the relevant time -- relevant time to the indictment. We heard from the witness that the KU register and probably none of the -- of the log-books normally kept in the SJB cannot be located. So I would be grateful for the instruction of the Trial Chamber in which way should I proceed, if -- if I should proceed at all with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, there probably are better witnesses then for seeking to admit this kind of evidence, witness who probably can talk more about the documents that he intends to show this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, we are not unmindful of the potential relevance of the evidence that you wish to lead, but our difficulty is that -- notwithstanding the present responsibilities of this witness, whether there is a better witness who can -- who can prove the documents on which you wish to rely, because it seems to us that taken at its highest, all the witness can -- can tell us is that having the over -- having the current overall responsibility, the custodian of these records, this is something that should have happened 20 years ago. So where does that leave us? Mr. Olmsted's point is that -- as I understand it, is that he accepts the relevance of where you're going, but there must be a better witness who can establish the link.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand and appreciate, Your Honours. Your Honours, I see the time. What I'm proposing to do, if there is no objection from the Office of the Prosecutor, that I -- I give the set of documents to the witness which pertain to the municipality of Sanski Most, and that is the KU register that he has reviewed. It -- it refers to documents listed as tab number 4 until tab number 12, so nine documents altogether, and I propose to give these documents to the witness so he can verify if these documents -- if any of these documents are, in fact, in the KU register and, therefore, in his diagram, and he can inform us tomorrow. And if some of the documents are not, I will just make the reference to them and -- and that is how I'm going to finish my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And that should save us some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No. The only thing is, of course he can -- he has his annexes with him so he can certainly compare the documents to his findings in his annexes. As far as the log-book from Sanski Most itself, I'm not sure, do we want to get that to him? Is that necessary for the purposes of what my learned friend wants to do? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it would depend on the witness. It guess that it would be better if the witness would be provided with the log-book from Sanski Most so he can be in a position to verify these documents so we'll lose minimum time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the usher will pass them on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, we are about to take the adjournment -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, we are about to take the adjournment for the day. Your testimony is not yet quite at an end. Mr. Zecevic is winding up his cross-examination, he having exhausted the time allotted to him, but he will be with you briefly for tomorrow and then Mr. Krgovic. So we have a few matters with which to deal before we rise, so the usher will escort you from the courtroom and we will resume tomorrow morning in this courtroom at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We crave the indulgence of the interpreters and the rest of the support staff, although we notice it's past the time for the adjournment, we understand the Prosecution has a few matters to raise. But before they do that, we wish to issue an oral corrigendum to the order that was made today in respect of Witness 023, and that is the documents may be added to the 65 ter list, and through oversight, one number was omitted, and that number is 10397, which should now be regarded as incorporated into that order. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. In view of the time, I'll just raise one and ask to raise the other one tomorrow. The most pressing relates to a discussion that was had Tuesday afternoon with Ms. Korner when you were having the discussions about scheduling witnesses and problems that happened with estimates of cross-examination. We had made a request asking Your Honours to possibly reduce the gap from six weeks to four weeks, during which we could call witnesses who are going to appear to testify about the adjudicated facts, and I think Judge Hall at page 13642 indicated that you would discuss and revert to the parties at the next sitting. I don't know if you had an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I raise it now because Ms. Pidwell and I are meeting with victim witnesses this afternoon to speak about scheduling issues [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we wish to be heard on the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think you were heard, and for -- for the record at this point, the Chamber has discussed the issue of the six weeks' delay, and we discussed it in the context -- in the broader context of seeking to avoid times in court where no witness is available, and so we will hand down our decision on that major issue, but for the limited purpose of -- of altering the six weeks delay, the Chamber's position is that we will not allow this. So the six weeks still is the delay that we will work with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And tomorrow morning if I may raise another issue concerning something that Mr. Krgovic raised today. We may resolve it during the evening. If not, I'd like a chance to address it in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment until 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of August, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
